title: Exam Question Patterns and Strategy
shortDescription: How each English question TYPE is usually structured and how to approach it under time pressure — strategy, not predictions about exact future questions.
genZNote: Same subject, different disguises every year. Learn the pattern behind the pattern and the disguise stops mattering.

sections.heading: Why 'pattern' rather than 'prediction'
sections.body: This section describes commonly tested QUESTION FORMATS and how to approach each one strategically — it does not, and cannot, predict the exact questions a future exam will contain. Treat every point here as 'commonly tested pattern', never as a guarantee.

sections.heading: Question format → what it tests → fastest approach

rows: Fill in the blank
Grammar rule or contextual vocabulary
Read the full sentence first; identify the missing word's job before looking at options
Error spotting
A specific grammar-rule violation in one part
Run the agreement → tense → preposition → pronoun → article → parallelism checklist
Sentence improvement
Best grammatical phrasing among near-identical options
Treat the original as a valid option; pick the most correct AND most natural phrasing
Synonym/Antonym
Precise meaning and connotation, not just a rough match
Fix the word's exact sense/part of speech in context before comparing options
One-word substitution
A precise single word for a descriptive phrase
Identify the theme (person/place/fear/study) and check root words (-phobia, -logy, -phile)
Idioms and phrases
Conventional (not literal) meaning
Never choose an option that just restates the idiom's literal words
Sentence rearrangement
Logical/chronological ordering and cohesion
Find the true opening sentence first via pronoun/connector clues, then build pairs
Cloze test
Grammar + vocabulary sustained across a passage
Read the whole passage once before attempting any blank; keep tense/tone consistent
Voice transformation
Correct passive/active conversion by tense
Identify the active sentence's exact tense before applying that tense's passive formula
Narration transformation
Correct direct-to-indirect conversion rules
Identify sentence type (statement/question/command) before applying its specific template

sections.heading: General time-management strategy
bullets: Attempt the question TYPES you're fastest at first (often vocabulary and one-word substitution, since they need recall rather than multi-step reasoning) to bank quick marks.

For error-spotting and sentence-improvement questions, don't over-analyse a sentence that 'sounds fine' after one careful checklist pass — extended hesitation rarely improves accuracy on these formats.
In cloze/rearrangement questions (which take longer to read), do them in one focused pass rather than switching back and forth with other questions, since re-establishing context costs time.

sections.heading: Using elimination effectively
bullets: Eliminate any option that is grammatically wrong FIRST, even if its meaning seems appealing — a grammar error disqualifies an option outright in most formats.
Among grammatically valid options, eliminate the one(s) that clash with the connotation, tense, or tone already established by the sentence/passage.
If exactly two options remain and both seem correct, re-check for a redundancy, parallelism, or preposition-collocation issue — these are the most common 'tie-breaker' differences examiners build in.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Each English question format tests a specific, recurring skill combination — recognising the format and applying its matching strategy is faster and more reliable than reading every question from scratch.
keyFacts: Commonly tested pattern, not a guarantee of exact future content — never treat any 'expected question' claim as certain.
Elimination by grammar correctness first, then by tone/connotation fit, resolves most close-call questions.

highYieldFacts: Grammar correctness eliminates options faster and more reliably than trying to judge 'which sounds better' first.
commonTraps: Spending equal time on every question type regardless of personal speed/accuracy on that format.
Treating any single practice question as evidence of exactly what will appear in the real exam.
mustRemember: Match the question format to its known approach immediately, rather than solving each question as if seeing the format for the first time.
possibleQuestions: This section is strategy-focused; practice applying its checklists to fresh questions in each format above rather than expecting fixed sample answers.
